newsitem.title: KENYA: Hutu infiltrators kill in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Hutu infiltrators kill in Rwanda.

text.p: Hutu hardliners, some infiltrating Rwanda among a million returning refugees, have carried out massacres inside the country as well as crossborder raids, Rwandan government and aid sources said on Tuesday.
Up to 50 people, including Rwandan soldiers, civilians and armed infiltrators from Zaire, have been killed since Christmas, a Rwandan defence spokesman and aid sources said.

The incidents show that a low-level conflict between Rwanda's Tutsi-dominated army and Hutus linked to the former government army goes on despite the fall in October and November of Hutu bases in eastern Zaire refugee camps.
On Sunday night nine people, including seven children, were killed in Gitarama, southern Rwanda, by former members of Hutu militias, Rwandan army spokesman Emmanuel Ndahiro said.
Aid sources said former Hutu militia also killed some 15 people in a bar in Taba commune, south of the capital Kigali, in the last week of December.
"They walked in armed, told everybody inside to put their money and their hands on the tables, then shot 15 of them in the face and back," said one aid source.
Aid workers also said eight people were killed by heavy fire from across the Zairean border in an attack on northwestern Ruhengeri province between December 26 and 28.
"Although infiltration is not a huge problem we can't exclude or discount the bad intentions of some of those who came home with the refugees," said Rwandan presidential adviser Claude Dusaidi.
More than half a million Rwandan refugees have returned home since Rwandan-backed rebels broke up refugee camps in eastern Zaire in October and November and seized control of a swath of territory.
Ndahiro, speaking by telephone from Kigali, said army soldiers raided three houses in Ruhengeri on Saturday night.
"There were infiltrators from Zaire inside who came out at dawn and exchanged fire with our troops. We killed eight of them. The search is still on for the culprits. We lost one soldier," he said.

Rwandan state radio said the infiltrators had been hiding for up to 10 days to try to release prisoners from a nearby jail and said an unknown number of civilians were also killed. At least 12 other people were killed in the same area in the last two weeks, Radio Rwanda reported on Monday.
"What we are experiencing is killings by infiltrators, militias and former soldiers to remind us they still exist," Ndahiro said.

Hutu militants responsible for the genocide of around 800,000 people were driven into Zaire and Tanzania by Tutsi forces in the summer of 1994. They were dealt another crushing blow when they were ejected from their bases in eastern Zaire refugee camps late last year.
Thousands fled west deeper into Zaire unwilling to return and face Rwandan justice but others returned home with more than a million Rwandan Hutus from Zaire and Tanzania.
Tanzanian soldiers pushed home hundreds of thousands more refugees from inside their borders in December.

United Nations human rights observers reported in Geneva on Tuesday that Rwandan authorities had detained 5,460 refugees returning to their homeland between November 15 and the end of the year in connection with the 1994 genocide.

The observers also gave details of seven deaths in five incidents between December 20 and 26 in southeasterly Kibungo prefecture, where tension is high between the local population and Hutu returnees.
Rwanda has started trials against those suspected of taking part in the genocide and passed the first two death sentences in a Kibungo court on January 3.
